title: Convert two prose-only assertion rules into enforced machinery (registered assertion fields; the free-text/capture verbatim rule)
objective: Two rules this product depends on exist only as prose that a future contributor can silently violate. (1) An HtmlTextAssertion may pin ANY field name; the closed-vocabulary check is a dict lookup that SILENTLY SKIPS an unregistered name, so a mistyped or invented field escapes validation and is then re-read downstream as a quota metric. (2) docs/PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md states that free-text values must reproduce the asserted source wording verbatim, and every capture.json claims its pinned blocks occur exactly once in the committed bytes -- both carried by builder discipline and evaluator review, neither by code. Convert both placeholders into deterministic failures without changing what any of the six merged providers extracts or classifies.
measured_premise: P1 MEASURED: base re-derived with `git ls-remote origin main` = 5a3fb24debb502544a0aa952ff39a7d306970a85, equal to this worktree's HEAD and to the SHA the brief stated. Confirmed rather than trusted.
P2 MEASURED baseline, offline (no DATABASE_URL): `python -m pytest -q` -> 2426 passed, 244 skipped, exit 0.

P3 MEASURED the silent skip, read in apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/html.py __post_init__: `allowed = _ASSERTION_CLOSED_VALUES.get(assertion.field)` followed by `if allowed is not None and ...`. When the field is not one of the four registered names the branch is skipped entirely -- not warned, not logged. That is rule (1)'s exact defect.

P4 MEASURED the downstream consequence, read in apps/api/app/publish/revalidate.py: NON_QUOTA_FIELDS is the registry of reserved semantic fact fields, and `revalidate_quotas` treats EVERY other fact key as a quota metric. So an unregistered assertion field does not merely fail to validate -- it is silently PUBLISHED as a quota row, while the material condition its name resembles stays absent.

P5 MEASURED the control-plane hazard: HtmlDocAdapter._rejected writes facts {'error', 'detail'} and validate() treats a candidate carrying 'error' as rejected. 'provider' and 'quotas' are likewise adapter/publisher plumbing. Nothing today stops an assertion pinning any of those four names, which would let a profile forge or mask a rejection.

P6 MEASURED the field vocabulary actually in use across all 35 registered HTML profiles: 96 distinct assertion field names, 102 matrix field names, 23 column field names. An enumerated closed list of ALL fact fields is therefore NOT the design and would turn every merged provider red. Only the RESERVED half is bounded; quota metrics are open by construction.

P7 MEASURED which reserved fields the six providers actually assert: eligibility (13 profiles), exhaustion_behaviour (21), has_paid_dependencies (4), notes, offer_type, requires_card, service. The other 89 assertion fields are quota metrics.

P8 MEASURED value types: across every assertion on every registered profile, ZERO non-string values occur on a non-reserved (quota-metric) field. Requiring a string value there is therefore satisfied by all six providers today.

P9 MEASURED the verbatim question, and the naive form of the rule is WRONG. Comparing assertion.value against assertion.text for containment flags 13 of the six providers' assertions. TEN are `service` (a canonical identity name such as 'AWS 12 Month Free Tier'), and three are quota-metric normalisations ('1' from 'exactly one free database'). Those are MAPPINGS from evidence to a canonical value, exactly like offer_type -- not free text. docs/PROVIDER_ADAPTERS.md scopes the rule precisely: 'Free-text values that reach the UI, such as `notes`, must reproduce the asserted source wording verbatim.' Scoped to declared free-text fields the violation count is ZERO.

P10 MEASURED the capture-grounding question with the engine's OWN _DocumentCollector (the same representation the extractor sees, not a substring scan of raw bytes): across all 31 html sources declared by the six provider YAMLs, EVERY pinned assertion text occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the declared scope of its committed capture. Anomalies: 0. Missing captures: 0. So the rule can be enforced with no false rejection on correct work.

P11 MEASURED that today ZERO assertions are `required=False`. The optional path (`if not matches: ... continue`) is therefore an untravelled silent-skip that a future slice could reach, which is why the capture-grounding guard must cover optional assertions too.

P12 MEASURED the before-verdicts of all six providers, DB-free, by driving the real HtmlDocAdapter over each committed capture and then the real revalidate_quotas + classify_offer path the publisher uses in memory: 31 sources, 31 candidates, 0 validation problems. Report digest sha256 31274d8de1509f3d7baaaa57055d91af2fa3574357ec26af821a26421c13d632.

acceptance_criteria: AC1 An assertion pinning an UNREGISTERED field is REJECTED at profile construction, with a message naming the offending field AND the registered vocabulary.
AC2 PAIRED CONTROL: an assertion pinning a REGISTERED field, identical in every other respect, is ACCEPTED. Without this the rejection could be a profile that fails for any reason.
AC3 The four adapter/publisher control-plane names (error, detail, provider, quotas) are refused outright, so a profile cannot forge or mask a rejection.
AC4 A reserved field asserted with a wrongly-typed value is REJECTED (booleans stay booleans; closed vocabularies stay closed).
AC5 A COMPOSED or PARAPHRASED free-text value is REJECTED at profile construction.
AC6 PAIRED CONTROL: the genuine verbatim quotation of the same block is ACCEPTED.

AC7 Every pinned assertion text of every html source declared by the six provider YAMLs occurs EXACTLY ONCE, in its declared scope, in its committed capture -- measured with the engine's own _DocumentCollector, not a raw-bytes substring scan.
AC8 The capture-grounding guard covers OPTIONAL assertions, which the runtime path silently skips.
AC9 ALL SIX MERGED PROVIDERS CLASSIFY EXACTLY AS ON main. The 31-source verdict report is re-derived before and after and the two are byte-identical (digest comparison, not eyeballing).

AC10 Every new test is proved NON-VACUOUS by mutation: prediction recorded BEFORE the run, baseline GREEN, the guarded thing broken, RED observed, restored byte-exactly and proved restored by `git hash-object`, never by `git diff --numstat`.
AC11 Each mutation prints the patched line and asserts its anchor matched EXACTLY ONCE, so a mutation that did not apply cannot be mistaken for a control that did not fire.
AC12 Full offline suite stays green and the collected test count strictly increases with none lost.
AC13 Protected state verified by `git hash-object` blob comparison against base, never by `git diff --numstat`.
verification_commands: python -m ruff check . ; python -m ruff format --check .
git hash-object <protected paths> compared against git rev-parse <base>:<path>
negative_and_regression_tests: Unregistered field -> ValueError naming the field and the vocabulary; registered field -> constructs (paired).
error / detail / provider / quotas pinned -> ValueError (control-plane names).
requires_card='no' (string not bool) -> ValueError; requires_card=False -> constructs (paired).
notes paraphrased / truncated / stitched from two blocks -> ValueError; the exact block -> constructs (paired).
Capture grounding over all 31 declared sources; a deliberately reworded needle proves the walk is not vacuous.
31-source before/after verdict digest equality for aws, azure, gcp, github, oracle, vercel.

data_security_privacy_portability_z0.data: No migration, no schema change, no fixture edited. Additive validation only.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.security_privacy: No secret introduced. The internal package-feed hostname used by this machine's toolchain is never written to any repository file, commit message, PR body or report. Zero socket operations are added; tests/unit/test_no_live_fetcher_in_tests.py keeps enforcing that by AST.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.portability: No new runtime dependency and no new mandatory service. Standard library only.
data_security_privacy_portability_z0.z0: Both rules guard the evidence path that produces a Z0 verdict. The failure mode being closed is an unsupported claim that a service is free -- either because a mistyped material condition silently vanished into a quota row, or because a quotation was composed rather than quoted. Enforcement is FAIL-CLOSED at construction: a profile that cannot prove its pins is refused rather than allowed to extract.

evaluation_level_rationale: Level 2 is mandatory: this touches provider adapters, evidence extraction, and the inputs to Z0 classification at once.
boundary: Draft PR only. Do not merge. Do not modify agent-state/feature_list.json.
